guards.what: G1 (LIVE): no card reward option is ever Swift-enchanted, and BOTH halves of the stub's premise are false
guards.issue: MECHANISM: wing_charm.py declares only id/name/rarity and its docstring justifies that with 'the sim has no enchantments or card rewards, so this is a no-op stub'. PROMPT.md bug class 12 applied, and the premise is false twice over. (a) The sim HAS enchantments: enchantments.py defines 19 of them including SwiftEnchantment (enchantments.py:341-357), and the ported relic/beautiful_bracelet attaches Swift through it. (b) The sim HAS card rewards and the exact hook: rewards.create_reward_cards runs `relic.modify_card_reward_options(run, cards)` over every run relic (rewards.py:297-301). .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep C lists this unit under BOTH the 'no enchantments' and the 'out-of-combat reward modifier' premise families and reports a LIVE dispatch site for each. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py rewardstubs): a MONSTER card reward comes out as [('setup_strike', None), ('bludgeon', None), ('true_grit', None)] both with and without the relic; the same probe reports `SwiftEnchantment ported: 'swift'` and `can_enchant(strike)=True`. The CONTROL is decisive: relic/glitter implements the SAME C# hook -- TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate (Glitter.cs) -- and its port at sts2_rl/relics/glitter.py:16-21 turns the same three options into [('setup_strike','glam'), ('bludgeon','glam'), ('true_grit','glam')]. So the pipeline is not merely present but already used by a ported relic to enchant card reward options, which is precisely what this relic must do. Both sides ported: Shop rarity (buyable in every act), card rewards on every combat. Observable in RL play (a free draw-3 on a rewarded card) and in the deck the conformance runner compares. PROMPT.md bug class 29 checked, not assumed: glitter enchants EVERY eligible option and is not one-shot, silken_tress enchants every option once, and wing_charm enchants exactly ONE at random -- three deliberately different relics on one hook, so glitter's implementation is a template for the pipeline, not for the behaviour. Rule 7: enchantments.py, rewards.py, sts2_rl/relics/base.py, sts2_rl/relics/glitter.py, sts2_rl/relics/beautiful_bracelet.py, Glitter.cs and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.issue: PROMPT.md bug class 25. C# guarantees that every plain-pass modifier has finished before any Late modifier runs; the sim's single `for relic in list(run.relics)` loop (rewards.py:297-301) makes that registration-order luck. The census matters here: an executed grep of the game source finds exactly ONE plain-pass implementer, LastingCandy (LastingCandy.cs), and NINE Late implementers -- FresnelLens, FrozenEgg, Glitter, LavaLamp, MoltenEgg, SilkenTress, SilverCrucible, ToxicEgg and WingCharm. So the ordering that C# protects is 'Lasting Candy's Power-card substitution happens before anything enchants or upgrades the options'. DORMANT twice over today: wing_charm does nothing, and sts2_rl/relics/lasting_candy.py is ALSO a behaviourless stub (batch 8 audited it), so there is currently no plain-pass sim listener for a Late one to run ahead of. Fixing either one alone leaves it dormant; fixing both without adding the pass structure makes it live. Rule 7: Hook.cs, rewards.py, LastingCandy.cs, sts2_rl/relics/lasting_candy.py and audit/records/relic/lasting_candy.json are NOT hashed by this record.
